title: Different Doors
description: This dataset contains EEG recordings from forty participants performing a gambling task involving repeated door selections and monetary feedback. Blocks were either learnable, where one door yielded rewards more frequently, or unlearnable, where outcomes were randomly drawn but matched in overall win/loss totals. After each block, participants completed a brief survey on perceived learning, enjoyment, motivation, and performance. The dataset supports investigation of decision-making and reward learning processes reflected in EEG signals.
methods_description: Forty participants completed 20 blocks of 20 trials each, choosing between two doors and receiving feedback of monetary gain or loss. Ten blocks were learnable (one door had a 60% win rate, the other 10%) and ten were unlearnable (outcomes randomly drawn from learnable blocks but matched in totals). Each block was followed by a survey on door preference, enjoyment, motivation, and performance.
